feature: op6893 DPMAIF downlink: fragment ring and vendor MTU, plus what the modem image says about its own IP stack

image.note: flashed and booted; the fragment ring and MTU change ran on hardware

fragment_ring.what: the packet and fragment BAT rings share BAT_INIT_CON0/CON1 but latch separately, selected by the BAT_INIT_FRG_INIT bit, and the fragment buffers are added with the DL_BAT_FRG_ADD doorbell bit
implemented: a second BAT ring with CCCI_DPMAIF_DL_FRG_BUF_SZ buffers, published the same way
dpmaif_dl_bat_program() now takes a frag flag and latches ALLSET|EN or ALLSET|FRG_INIT|EN
dpmaif_dl_queue_enable() takes a frag flag so both latches are told the enable bit is on, and teardown tells both it is off
the fragment AO thresholds are configured rather than cleared: feature bit on, buffer size 1920, check threshold 62
fragment_ring.why_the_earlier_attempt_failed: the previous try programmed a fragment ring without BAT_INIT_FRG_INIT, so the fragment latch was never selected; the PIT handshake then reported a length error

mtu.change: the downlink MTU is now the vendor value 3080 instead of the BAT buffer size 1664
mtu.correction: DPMAIF_HW_PKT_BIDCNT is 1 in the vendor source (the comment reads '3-->1 should be 1 in E1'), so the earlier note that the vendor uses 3 was wrong and BID_MAXCNT was already correct

modem_image_ip_stack.how: the plaintext string tables inside the md1img partition are readable even though the code is not
found: driver/dpmaif/src/dpmaif_dev.c and driver/dpmaif/arch/97/src/dpmaif_dev_arch97_md.c, plus dpmaif_lisr_handler, dpmaif_dataflow_lisr_handler and DPMAIF_HISR
middleware/hif/ipfcore/core/src/{ipfc_core_available_seat,ipfc_core_meta,ipfc_core_private_room,ipfc_core_restaurant}.c and the dl_filter and rqos plugins
the interface name format string ccmni%d
modem_image_ip_stack.meaning: the modem runs a full IP middleware with per-interface sessions, filters and a buffer pool between the DPMAIF driver and the protocol stack, so a packet can be accepted by the transport and then dropped inside that middleware

embind_negative.idea: the image also contains AT+EMBIND with L2P values M-CCMNI, M-RNDIS, M-MBIM and M-LHIF, which looked like the missing step that binds a PDP context to the CCMNI layer-2 path
embind_negative.measured: AT+EMBIND? returns +EMBIND: 0, so nothing is bound; AT+EMBIND=? returns only the template (0,1),(list of supported <L2P>s),(1-16) without enumerating the strings; AT+EMBIND=1,"M-CCMNI",1, AT+EMBIND=1,1,1 and AT+EMBIND=1 all return ERROR
embind_negative.conclusion: the command is not usable over this AT channel, so it is not a lever available to this bring-up
embind_negative.caveat: this says nothing about whether the binding itself matters; it only says this interface cannot set it

not_proven: whether the modem forwards uplink frames, and where inside ipcore/dpfm a drop would happen
why the engine never takes a downlink buffer
what the modem needs before it will deliver a packet on this ring
